summary: Frontend-only testing of the Next.js 15 Physiogen marketing site to verify the hydration mismatch fix (removed formatDetection metadata, added static format-detection meta, added suppressHydrationWarning). All critical checks PASSED. Homepage loads on both desktop (1920x800) and mobile (390x844 with iOS Safari UA); hero heading 'Guaranteed Pain Relief' renders in both viewports (screenshots confirm). ZERO React hydration errors/warnings observed in browser console across homepage, /clinical-case-studies, and /clinical-case-studies/CS000001. Only benign warnings present: woff2 font preload not-used-within-window-load (Next.js font optimization heuristic, not a bug) and a couple of SVG preload notices on case studies. Exactly one <meta name='format-detection'> tag present with content 'telephone=no, date=no, address=no, email=no'. Mobile hamburger opens the nav drawer with all links. Phone/WhatsApp CTAs present (8 links including tel:00923137818887 and https://wa.me/923137818887). All three tested routes return HTTP 200. No Next.js dev error dialog present on mobile.

issues: 'Special Promotion' modal auto-opens on load and covers the hero on first paint; consider delaying it or making it dismissible via ESC + backdrop click. Not a bug, minor UX.

Consider adding data-testid attributes to key elements (hero heading, mobile menu toggle, phone/WhatsApp CTAs, promo modal close) to make future automated regression tests more robust.
context_for_next_testing_agent: This is a pure Next.js 15 App Router app at /app (not the standard React+FastAPI stack). Runs via next dev on port 3000. Test URL: https://534b4735-6e64-4da7-8e77-8e3bbd196567.preview.emergentagent.com . A 'Special Promotion' modal auto-opens on the homepage and can obstruct selectors — dismiss it (button[aria-label*='close']) before interacting with hero content. Hero heading text spans two lines/spans ('Guaranteed' + 'Pain Relief'); use screenshot verification or evaluate innerHTML rather than innerText contains.
rca of the issue: Original hydration mismatch was caused by iOS Safari's format-detection auto-linking of phone numbers/emails/addresses/dates injecting <a> tags into SSR-rendered content, changing the DOM before React hydrated. Fix removed the conflicting formatDetection metadata block from layout.tsx, added a single explicit <meta name='format-detection' content='telephone=no, date=no, address=no, email=no'> to disable all auto-linking uniformly, and added suppressHydrationWarning on <html>/<body> as a safety net. Verified: zero hydration console messages under iOS Safari UA on 390x844 viewport.
